$comment: Cursor's docs now present `agent` as the primary command, but the installer still ships `cursor-agent` and `agent` is far too generic a name to probe for (`command -v agent` can false-positive on unrelated binaries). `cursor-agent` remains supported as the stable alias, so it is both the probe target and the launch binary.

modelSelection.$comment: Cursor's model roster is subscription-entitlement-dependent and churns often, so no ids are seeded — the user adds the models their plan actually has via Settings (the no-guess policy from BUNDLED_AGENT_MODEL_CATALOGS applies to the manifest seed here too).

resume.$comment: Cursor documents `--resume <chat-id>` and `--continue` (previous session). Mirrors the OpenCode wiring: --continue as the base, the explicit resume pair only when the caller has an id. Unverified end-to-end, so capabilities.resumeSession stays false until confirmed against a real install (MC-1464/MC-1465 discipline).

mcpConfig.$comment: Cursor reads workspace MCP servers from .cursor/mcp.json in the same {"mcpServers": {...}} shape Claude Code uses, so the claude-code writer applies as-is.

capabilities.$comment: resumeSession is intentionally false pending end-to-end verification (MC-1464/MC-1465 discipline); the resume argv above is wired for the flip. sessionIdFromCaller is false because Cursor mints its own chat ids (no --session-id-style launch assignment is documented).
